classes.name: Z-drug hypnotics
classes.description: Zolpidem IR/ER/SL (Ambien, Ambien CR, Edluar), eszopiclone (Lunesta), zaleplon; ramelteon (Rozerem) and low-dose doxepin (Silenor) may be listed as alternatives.
classes.plainDescription: A bedtime pill for trouble falling or staying asleep.

classes.name: Orexin receptor antagonists
classes.description: Dual orexin receptor antagonists: suvorexant (Belsomra), lemborexant (Dayvigo), daridorexant (Quviviq).
classes.plainDescription: A newer bedtime pill that blocks the brain's wake signal.

classes.name: Benzodiazepines and buspirone for anxiety
classes.description: Benzodiazepines (alprazolam IR/ER, lorazepam, clonazepam, diazepam, chlordiazepoxide, clorazepate) and the non-benzodiazepine anxiolytics buspirone and hydroxyzine as alternatives.
classes.plainDescription: A medicine for anxiety or panic attacks.

records.verificationNote: verified. PDL p.46 lists Belsomra, Dayvigo and Quviviq under the NON-PREFERRED heading with no PA flag printed; CF p.246 shows Belsomra '#' (carved out) and CF p.245 shows Dayvigo '#'. Quviviq not on CF text reviewed. Suvorexant chosen as the most established agent in the class (no lower-barrier DORA is printed). Not preferred status is recorded as a restriction because no PA is printed either way; no PA inferred. [Sonnet check 2026-11-02: Carved out to FFS (CF '#', pp.245-246), so the Single PDL governs: Belsomra, Dayvigo and Quviviq are listed under NON-PREFERRED (PDL p.46) with no PA printed. The PDL says only that preferred agents need no PA. On the CF the PDL-NP flag almost always travels with PA (about 2,000 of 2,286 PDL-NP lines), and non-formulary requests go through PA (CF p.3), so PA by exception is likely but is not printed for DORAs; left out of paRequired, cell set to partial.]
